activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Maria went to the music studio. The room was hot. The teacher, Miss Anna, opened the window. A little breeze came in.

Maria sat at the big piano. "I want to play the lion song," she said. "The lion roars."

Maria pressed one key. The sound was very quiet. The lion sounded like a tiny mouse. She pressed the key again, soft and slow. Still tiny. "Oh no," said Maria.

Miss Anna smiled. "Try again," she said. Maria pressed the key hard and fast. Boom! The sound was big and loud. "The lion is roaring!" said Maria. "I pressed hard, so it is loud. I pressed soft, so it was small."

She pressed soft, soft, then hard. "Little mouse, little mouse, big lion!" Maria laughed. Miss Anna clapped.

"Now let's build the whole song," said Miss Anna. Maria played soft for the mouse. She played hard for the lion. The song grew and grew. At the end, Maria pressed the key as hard as she could. "Roar!" she said.

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
story:
Abigail looked out the window. Snow was on the grass. Snow was on the swings. The park was white all over. "No park today," said Mama. "The snow closed it."

Abigail wanted to play outside anyway. She put on her boots. She put on her red coat. She clapped her mittens together. Then she held a snowball in her hands. The snowball got small. Then it was gone! Water ran down her mittens. "It turned to water," said Abigail. Her warm hands made the snow melt.

Abigail picked up another snowball. This time she did not hold it long. She set it on the step and patted it flat. Then she went inside and found her toy frog. She put the green frog on the windowsill. Soon the sun came out. The snow on the step got shiny, then wet, then it was gone too. "The sun melts it," said Abigail. Mama laughed and gave her cocoa. Abigail took a sip and watched the white park drip, drip, drip.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Ivy did not want a shot. She sat in the big chair at the doctor's office. "Can we go home now?" she asked. Mom said, "First, one little check. Then we go." A nurse came in with a small light. "Can you hold still?" she asked. "I will look at your eyes." Ivy held still. The light was bright. Her eyes saw it blink.

The nurse put headphones on Ivy's ears. "Tell me when you hear a beep." Ivy waited. She waited some more. Beep! "I hear it!" said Ivy. "My ears heard it first," she said. "The beep made my ears feel funny, so I talked." The nurse smiled. "That is just right."

Then the nurse held out an orange sticker. "Smell it," she said. Ivy's nose sniffed. "Orange!" she said. The nurse gave her a tiny taste of sweet syrup on a spoon. Ivy's tongue tasted it. "Sweet!" Last, the nurse touched Ivy's arm with a cotton ball. "Feel this," she said. Ivy's fingers felt it, soft like a kitten. "You used your whole body team," said the nurse. "Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands." Then it was shot time. Ivy squeezed Mom's hand. It was over fast. "All done," said the nurse. Ivy picked a pink bandage. "My eyes pick pink," she said.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Kayden ran to the big sports field. Mom and Dad and Grandma came too. "Look, the game is starting!" said Dad. The players kicked the ball fast. Everyone jumped up and waved.

"I want to play one day," said Kayden. "That is my dream!" He clapped his hands. He stomped his feet. "Go, go, go!" he shouted.

Then big gray clouds came. The wind blew and blew. Kayden shivered. "Brrr!" he said. "The wind makes cold weather," he told Grandma. Grandma smiled. She pulled a soft blanket from her bag. She wrapped it around Kayden. "Warm now!" he said.

The sun came back. The crowd cheered loud. The team kicked one more goal. "We won! We won!" everyone shouted. Kayden threw his arms up high.

A player ran over and waved at the crowd. Kayden waved back. "I saw you, little fan!" the player called. Kayden hugged his blanket tight and jumped up and down.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Isaac ran to the backyard with his toy stove. Today he would make a pretend feast for Mom and Dad. He put a red bowl on the stove. He stirred in dirt, water, and three yellow leaves. He gave his meal a name. "I will call it Backyard Soup!" he said.

Mom sat down at the little table. Dad came too. Isaac served the soup in red cups. But the soup was too runny. It ran right off the spoon. "Why is it so watery?" Isaac asked. He looked at his bowl. "Oh! I put in lots and lots of water," he said. "Just a little splash next time."

He stirred in more dirt, bit by bit. The soup got thick. It did not run off the spoon. It went pop, pop, pop with big air bubbles as he stirred. Isaac filled three bowls. Mom took a tiny pretend sip. Dad clapped his hands. "Backyard Soup for everyone!" said Isaac.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Luke ran into the storytime room. Today he would get his very own library card! It was round and blue, like a little moon. He got to wear it on a string around his neck.

Luke picked a book about seeds. A seed goes in the dirt. Then a plant grows up! He hugged the book tight.

"I want to keep it forever," said Luke.

The librarian shook her head with a smile. "You can take it home. Then you bring it back. Other kids want to read it too."

Luke read the seed book at bedtime. He read it at breakfast too. Then he ran back to the library.

"Here is my book!" he said. "I brought it back so someone else can read it."

Then he picked out three more.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Violet was on the swim team. Today was the big relay race at the pool. The water smelled like sunshine and chlorine. Her goggles felt tight on her little nose.

"Wait for Tom to touch the wall," said Coach May. "Then you jump in." Violet wondered why she had to wait. She stood on the edge and watched the water splash.

Tom swam fast. His arms went round and round. He came closer and closer. Violet jumped too soon! She hit the water before his hand touched the wall. Beep! The whistle blew. "Too early," said Coach May, kind and calm. "You dived before Tom touched. That is why we have to start again."

They tried again. Tom swam. His hand came near. Violet waited, waited, waited. Tap! His hand hit the wall. Then Violet jumped in. The water was cool on her skin. Her legs kicked and kicked. She touched the wall at the end, and her whole team cheered.

"A surprise!" said Tom. "We did it!" Violet laughed. "We take turns in the wall game," she said. And everyone jumped in for one big happy splash.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Everly ran into the big room. It was full of books. She picked a book about a red fire truck. "I want this one," she said. A lady at the desk gave Everly a little card. It was her very first library card. Everly held it tight.

"Can the book be mine forever?" Everly asked. "No," said the lady. "It is just for now." Everly made a sad face. "Then what?" she asked. "You take it home. Then you bring it back. Other kids want to read it too." The fan above the door began to blow on Everly's hair. Her hair went up like a bird. "My hair is flying!" she laughed.

Everly put the book in her bag. She waved to the fire truck book. "Bye bye," she said. "I will bring you back. But first you come home with me." She skipped out the door.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
Mackenzie was four today. She wore a big hat with a number four on it. Her family and friends came to the bowling alley with her.

First Mackenzie had to trade her shoes. "These shoes are too big," she said. "Big shoes help you not to slip," said Grandma. Mackenzie took the heavy ball. She threw it in the air. The ball went thump on the floor. It did not go near the pins. "Oh no," said Mackenzie.

Daddy knelt down beside her. "Try again," he said. "Let me help." He showed her how to swing her arms. This time Mackenzie let the ball touch the floor. The ball began to turn and turn. It rolled straight down the long floor. Crash! All ten pins fell down. "Hooray!" everyone shouted.

"I did it! I did it!" said Mackenzie. Her friend Ben clapped and clapped. Then it was Ben's turn. He rolled his ball too, and seven pins fell.

After the game, they ate pizza and cake. Mackenzie licked her lips. "My pizza is salty," she said with a giggle. Mommy gave her a cup of water. Then Daddy brought out a surprise. It was a pink cake with four candles. Mackenzie blew and blew. All the candles went out. "Make a wish," said Grandma. Mackenzie closed her eyes tight. Then she took one more big bite of cake.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Zayn ran to first base. His shoes slid in the dirt. Thud! He fell on his bottom. "Ow," he said. Coach Peppy blew her whistle. "Zayn, why did you slip?" Zayn looked at his shoes. "My shoes are smooth," he said. "The dirt is loose." Coach Peppy held up her own shoes. They had little bumps on the bottom. "These are cleats," she said. "The bumps dig into the dirt."

Zayn wanted to try them. At the next game, he wore his new cleats. The big clock above the field showed it was time to play. He hit the ball and ran. His feet did not slide one bit. The cleats went deep into the dirt and held on. "Safe!" said Coach Peppy. Zayn grinned at first base. "My shoes have little teeth now," he said. "Grrr!" His friend Ben laughed. "Silly shoes," said Ben. Zayn stomped his feet. "Roar!" he said, and they both giggled all the way to the dugout.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Emily sat in her bed. She had a book from the library. It was about a curly sheep. Emily wanted to keep it forever.

Dad came in. "Time to read," he said.

Emily opened the book. She pointed at the marks. "Dad, what are those?" Dad read them out loud. The marks said, "Sheep sleeps on a hill." Emily gasped. "The marks talk!"

"Yes," said Dad. "Now turn the pages this way." He showed her. The story went front to back.

They read slowly. They read all the sheep pages. Dad said, "We must take it back on Friday. Other kids will read it too."

Emily held the book to her chest. She did not want to. She thought and thought.

Then she found paper and a pen. "Dad, draw the sheep words for me." Dad wrote, "Sheep sleeps on a hill." Emily put the paper under her pillow.

"Now I will always remember the sheep," she said.

Dad opened the window a little. Cool air came in. He kissed her head.

On Friday, Emily put the book in her bag. At the library, the sheep book went into the bin. Emily waved. "Bye, sheep. Someone else will read you now."

A boy picked it up right away. He opened it front to back. Emily smiled at him.

"He reads the marks too," she said.

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
story:
Beatrice woke up and saw white. Snow was on the window. Snow was on the grass. "No school today," said Dad. "It snowed too much, so school is closed." Beatrice gasped. A snow day at home!

They went to the big sledding hill. Beatrice went down, down, down. Whee! Then she wanted to feed the birds. She looked under the snow for a worm. She dug and dug. No worm! The ground was cold and hard, so the worms were hiding deep down. Beatrice laughed. "Silly worms! They are sleepy today."

A little bird hopped near her sled. It looked at her mitten. Beatrice shared her bread crumbs instead. The bird pecked them up fast. Then it sat right on the sled, like a tiny rider. "Your turn," said Beatrice. "Hold on tight!"

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Rowan was in the backyard with his dad. He saw a little brown bird by the fence. "Dad, the bird is hungry," said Rowan. "I will feed it."

Rowan ran to his toy box. He got his play apple and his play bread. He put them on the grass. The bird hopped close. Then the bird did not eat them. The bird flew away.

"Maybe toys are not food," said Rowan. His dad smiled. "Let's get real seeds," said Dad. They got seeds from the kitchen. They put the seeds on the grass. The bird came back. It pecked the seeds. Peck, peck, peck.

"The bird eats real food, not toys," said Rowan. "Toys are for playing." Then Rowan took his toy blocks. He made a big stack of blocks. The bird ate seeds. Rowan played with toys. Dad sat nearby in the warm sun.

Rowan looked at the bird. "Eat more, little bird," he said.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Everly sat in a big chair at the doctor's office. She had a stuffy nose. The doctor gave her a cookie to share. Everly took a little bite. "It tastes like nothing," she said.

She looked at the cookie with her eyes. It was brown and round. She sniffed it with her nose. But her nose was all plugged up. She could not smell it at all.

Everly pinched her nose shut. She took another bite. Still no taste! Then she let go of her nose. She heard the doctor say, "Take a big breath." Everly sniffed and sniffed. Slowly, her nose opened up a tiny bit.

She took one more bite. "Yum! Now it tastes sweet!" Everly was not angry anymore. She clapped her hands. "My nose helps my mouth taste," she said. The doctor read her chart and smiled. "That's right, Everly."

Everly touched the cookie with her fingers. It was bumpy and a little warm. She listened to the paper crinkle under her. "Can I have one more cookie, please?"

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Livia could not find her bunny. She looked in the toy box. No bunny. She looked under the table. No bunny. "Where did you go?" she asked.

Miss Rosa came to help. "Where did you play last?" she asked. Livia thought hard. "I played in the sand," she said. "Then I washed my hands." Miss Rosa smiled. "Then we look on the way back."

They walked down the hall. Livia spoke in a small voice. "Bunny, where are you?" Then she saw something spotted. It was her bunny's spotted ear, sticking out of a basket of towels! Livia picked it up and hugged it tight. "You were hiding near the towels because I dried my hands there," she said. Miss Rosa laughed. "You found it all by yourself." Livia held her bunny close and smiled all the way to snack time.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Anna stood in the band room. She held a big silver trumpet. "Now I will play it," she said. She blew and blew. But no sound came out. Just air. Just wind.

Her friend Tom laughed, but not mean. "You sound like a sleepy dragon," he said. Anna was not afraid. She tried again. Big air, small air, fast air. Still no sound.

Then the teacher picked up her own trumpet. Anna watched her lips. They went bzzz, like a bee. Anna tried the bee lips. Bzzz. Into the trumpet. Toot! A big sound came out.

"I know why now," Anna said. "My lips have to buzz first!" Tom clapped. Anna tooted again and again. "A bee lives in my trumpet," she said. "A hungry bee. It wants my cookie."

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Jaxon ran to the park. He saw the big red slide. He wanted to go first.

A girl was already at the ladder. "My turn," said Jaxon. "No," said the girl. "It is my turn now."

Jaxon stopped and looked. One girl was on the ladder. One boy was waiting behind her. They stood in a line. Why do they stand there? Jaxon wondered.

Jaxon walked to the back of the line. He waited. The girl went down. Whee! The boy went down. Whee! Then it was Jaxon's turn. He climbed up. He went down fast. It was fun!

"Again," said Jaxon. He went to the back of the line again. Waiting meant everyone got a turn. He saw that all by himself.

Next Jaxon found the water table. Splash! He put his hands in. A boy came over. "Can I splash too?" the boy asked. Jaxon moved over. They both splashed together. Two kids, one water table, room for both.

A turtle sat by the little pond. It looked strong and slow. "Hello, turtle," said Jaxon. The turtle slid into the water. Splash! Jaxon laughed.

The park helper rang a bell. All the kids came to the circle. Time for a story. Jaxon sat down too. Everyone sat. Everyone listened. Jaxon whispered, "I can follow the bell."

Then the story began, and Jaxon clapped his hands. "The end!" he said, "Again, again!"

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
story:
Mya stood at the school gate. The gate was huge. It was taller than Dad. Mya pushed it, but it did not move. "Why won't it open?" she asked. Dad said, "Let's look for a clue." Then Mya heard it. Ding, ding, ding! The bell rang inside. The gate clicked and swung open. "The bell opens the school!" said Mya.

Mya hugged her backpack. It had a horse on it. The horse had a red saddle. "One horse, two feet, three kisses for the horse," said Dad. He kissed the backpack three times. Mya laughed. "Silly Dad. Horses do not go to school." Then she looked at the gate. More kids came in. They did not push the gate. They all stood and waited. Ding, ding, ding! The bell rang again, and the gate clicked again. "See? No pushing," said Mya. "Just wait for the bell."

A boy named Sam ran to the gate. He pushed and pushed. The gate stayed shut. "It will not open!" said Sam. Mya held up her hand. "One, two, three," she counted. Ding, ding, ding! The gate swung wide open. Sam fell right through and landed on his bottom. "The bell did it," said Mya. "The bell says go!" Sam got up and dusted off his pants. "You are the bell boss," he said. Mya marched through the huge gate. "Come on, horse," she said. "School is open."

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Ryan ran into Miss Kim's music room. Today he would play the big piano. His tummy jumped with happy butterflies.

Miss Kim put Ryan's small hands on the keys. Ryan wanted to play fast, fast, fast. His fingers slipped and hit wrong notes. Bump, boom, blonk. He tried again. Wrong notes again.

"Why do I keep getting the wrong sounds?" Ryan asked. Miss Kim smiled. "Try it slow. Let's see."

Ryan played the notes very slowly. One, two, three, four. Each finger landed on its own key. Every note rang out clear. Then he played a little faster. Still clear!

"Slow hands help me pass the tricky part!" Ryan said. He played the song from the top. Slow first, then fast. Not one wrong note.

Miss Kim clapped. Ryan stood up tall. He felt so proud. "Can we do it one more time?" he asked.

"One more time," said Miss Kim. Ryan put his hands on the keys.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Zayn was a small boy on a big trip. The family had a hotel room. Zayn ran to the door. He pulled and pulled. The door did not open.

"My hands don't work!" said Zayn.

Daddy laughed. "Try the little card," he said. He gave Zayn the key card.

Zayn stood near the door. He put the card in the slot. The card had to slide in, then slide out. Beep! A little light turned green.

"The light said yes!" said Zayn.

He pushed the door. It opened! Mommy clapped. "The card made it open," said Zayn. "No card, no door. Yes card, yes door!"

Zayn tried again. Slide, beep, green light. "It opens because of the card!" he said.

The door swung wide. "Big room!" said Zayn. He ran in and jumped on the bouncy bed.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Arnaud was ready to sleep. He had his pajamas on. He had his teeth brushed. But he could not find his favorite cow. The cow was soft and white. Arnaud looked under the bed. He looked in the toy box. No cow. His mouth turned down. His eyes felt wet. "I feel sad," he said.

Then he saw a big shape by the curtain. It was tall and dark. Arnaud's tummy got tight. He pulled the blanket up high. "I feel scared," he whispered. He called, "Papa!"

Papa came in and turned on the little lamp. The dark shape was just Arnaud's coat on the chair. Arnaud sat up. "The dark made it look big," he said. "The light makes it look small." Papa smiled. "Yes. Light helps us see."

Then Papa lifted the coat. Something fell down with a soft plop. It was the white cow! Arnaud clapped his hands. He jumped up and down on the bed. "I feel excited!" he said. He hugged the cow tight.

Papa tucked him in again. Arnaud held the cow close. His eyes got heavy. He gave a big yawn. Papa turned off the lamp, but left the little one on. The room felt warm and soft. Arnaud patted the cow's head. "Night night, cow," he said. Then he closed his eyes and went to sleep.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Evelyn went to the park today. Yesterday the ice cream truck did not come. Evelyn wanted ice cream so much.

"Is the truck here now?" she asked Mama.

"Not now," said Mama. "The truck comes later, after lunch."

Evelyn looked down the road. It was empty. She heard only a bird. She waited. The road was still empty.

Evelyn picked a dandelion while she waited. She made it a present for Mama. "This is for you," she said.

"Thank you," said Mama. "Now we wait a little more."

Evelyn heard a song far away. It came closer and closer. Then the big white truck turned the corner. Evelyn's eyes went wide.

"The truck comes later, and now it is later!" Evelyn said. She clapped her hands.

Mama bought a little pink ice cream. Evelyn sat on the bench and licked it slowly.

"Tomorrow can we come again?" she asked.

"Yes," said Mama. "Tomorrow."

Evelyn smiled and took one more lick.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Jules ran to the garden with a big bag of seeds. "Today we plant!" he said. Grandpa gave him a small shovel. The sky was blue and warm. It did not snow today. That was good, because seeds like warm dirt.

Jules dug a little hole. He dropped a seed in. Then he patted the dirt down. He made ten holes in a row. He wanted big red tomatoes for lunch!

Jules waited. He looked at the dirt. Nothing happened. He waited more. Still nothing. "Where are my tomatoes?" he asked. The dirt was dry and cracked. A green frog hopped by. Even the frog looked thirsty!

Jules got his little watering can. He poured water on the dirt. He watered every single day. Then one morning, a tiny green leaf popped up! "The water helped!" Jules shouted. "Seeds need water to grow!" He jumped up and down. Day by day, more leaves came. Soon a small red tomato hung on the vine. Jules picked it and held it high. "Grandpa, look! My seed made lunch!"

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story:
Beatrice went to the mall with Mama. They walked past the toy shop. Then they came to a salon. A lady with scissors said, "First haircut?" Beatrice nodded. She did not feel bad. She felt big.

The lady put a big cape on Beatrice. Then she sprayed water on Beatrice's hair. Pss, pss. The wet hair stuck together in little lines. Beatrice looked in the mirror. "My hair sticks now," she said. Snip, snip went the scissors. The wet pieces fell and stuck to the cape. They did not go in her eyes or her mouth. Beatrice sat very still and waited.

At the end, the lady brushed her off. Mama unlocked the car with her key. Beatrice touched her short hair. "It got short because you cut the wet lines," she said. Mama smiled and buckled her in.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Elijah went to the store with Mom. He did not skip ahead today. He walked slow, holding her hand. Then he saw a small red shelf by the bread. It said LITTLE LIBRARY on top. Elijah knew those were words. Words say things you can read.

He found a book about a big yellow truck. The cover had a cute dog in the truck. Elijah opened the front. He turned the pages one by one, front to back. "It has words in it too," he said. "The words tell the truck story."

Mom read the little card in the back. It had a day on it. That day was the bring back day. Elijah held the truck book to his chest. He wanted to keep it forever. It was his dream book.

Then a girl came to the shelf. She looked and looked. She wanted the truck book too. Her face went sad. Elijah looked at her. He looked at his book. He looked at the card with the day on it.

"You can have a turn," he said. "I will bring it back on the card day. Then the book comes back here for you." The girl smiled big. Elijah smiled too. He carried the book to the front, nice and flat, so the pages would not bend. "See you soon, truck," he said.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
story:
Leah stood at the classroom door. She held a card with a letter on it. The letter was B. It looked hard to her.

"Is that a D?" said her friend Tom.

"No, it is a B," said Leah. "B says buh. B for banana!" She pretended to munch a big banana. "Buh, buh, buh."

Tom laughed. Then his sock began to slip down his foot. He pulled it up. "You munched the letter," he said. "Silly Leah."

The teacher called the next card. Leah looked at it. It was M. She knew this one. "M says mmm," she said. "Like when you eat something yummy!" She rubbed her tummy. "Mmm, mmm, mmm."

"You always make eating sounds," said Tom.

"That is my trick," said Leah. "The letter makes a sound. I make the sound too. Then I remember it!"

She held up the M card. It looked like two little mountains. "Mmm," she said, and marched around the table like a small mountain climber.

Tom marched too. "Mmm," he said. "This is fun."

At the door, the teacher smiled. "One more card, Leah."

Leah looked down. It was S. She wiggled like a snake. "Ssssss," she said.

Tom giggled so much his sock slipped again.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Abigail was at Grandma's house. She wanted to paint a green hill. Grandpa had red, blue and yellow paint. But there was no green paint at all. Where could green be hiding?

Abigail looked at the paints. She dipped her brush in blue. She made a blue hill. It was not right. She dipped her brush in yellow. She made a yellow sun. Still no green. Then some blue dripped onto the yellow sun. The spot turned green!

"Look, Grandma! Blue and yellow made green!" said Abigail. She mixed more blue and yellow together. She painted a big green hill with a friendly little rabbit on top. She painted red flowers too.

At nap time, Abigail had to sleep. But first she put her green painting by the window, so the rabbit could see the yellow sun. "Good night, rabbit," she whispered. "Sleep on your green hill."

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Elena was at Grandma's house. She could smell warm cookies. The cookie jar sat up high on a shelf. Elena wanted one very much.

She reached up. She reached and reached. The jar was too high. "Grandma, can you help me, please?" she asked. Grandma smiled. "What a nice way to ask," said Grandma. She lifted the jar down.

Elena hugged the jar. But her hands slipped. The lid fell and rolled under the chair. "Sorry, Grandma," said Elena. Grandma knelt down with her. "That is okay. Let us look together." They peeked under the chair. There was the lid! Elena picked it up. Grandma gave her a warm cookie. "Thank you, Grandma," said Elena.

Later it was time to swim. Grandpa blew fresh air into her swim ring. The water was cool on her toes. Elena splashed and laughed. The sun went down. "It is getting late," said Grandma. Elena climbed out. Grandma wrapped her in a big soft towel. "That cookie fell because my hands were slippery," said Elena. Grandma laughed and hugged her close. "More cookies tomorrow," she said.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Kinsley sat in her car seat. The sun was bright now. "Are we at Grandma's yet?" she asked. "Not yet," said Mama. "We get there later."

Kinsley looked out the window. A big truck went by. Then it was gone. "Now the truck is gone," said Kinsley. She held her book on her lap. It was the book Grandma read to her yesterday. Yesterday was the day before today.

"Will Grandma give me a peach?" asked Kinsley. "Tomorrow we can pick peaches," said Mama. "Today we just ride in the car." Kinsley watched the trees. She climbed her feet up onto the seat edge. The trees went by, one, two, three.

The car turned a corner. Grandma's house came into view. "We are here now!" said Kinsley. Grandma stood by the door. She held out a peach. It was big and juicy. "I got here because the car drove and drove," said Kinsley. She took a big bite.

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
story:
Henry was at Grandma's house. He had a cold. His nose ran and ran. Grandma gave him a big cup of water.

"I want to play," said Henry. He got up to run. His legs felt slow and wobbly. He sat back down on the soft couch. He drank more water. He drank the whole cup.

The sky outside was cloudy. Henry watched the clouds go by. He napped under a warm blanket. He woke up and drank more water. Then he blew his nose into a soft tissue.

Grandma went to the store. She came back with soup. Henry ate it all up. His nose did not run so much now. His legs did not feel wobbly.

"Can I play now?" Henry asked. Grandma smiled. "Just a little," she said. Henry walked to the toy box. He picked up his red truck. He rolled it slow and easy on the floor. Then he took a big drink of water and rolled the truck again.

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
story:
Jules had a cold. His nose was red. His voice had gone away. When he tried to talk, only a tiny sound came out. Jules wanted to say "more toast, please." But no words came.

Mom gave him warm water with honey. Jules took the spoon and did a slow dig into the honey jar. The honey dripped into his cup. It was sweet and warm. "Rest your voice," said Mom. "It will come back."

Jules closed his mouth. He kept it closed like a little door. He drank his warm water. He watched Dad cut an apple. He waited. He looked at the clock. The big hand moved a little bit. Then Jules tried again. "More toast, please," he said. His voice was back! Mom clapped her hands.

Then Dad opened his mouth to cheer. Nothing came out. Dad had caught the cold too. Dad pointed at the honey jar. Jules picked up the spoon and did a slow dig for Dad. "Now you wait," said Jules.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
Harper ran to the fence. A white sheep stood on the other side. "Hello, sheep!" she called. The sheep turned its head.

Grandpa gave Harper a small job. "Find five ways to meet the sheep," he said. Harper wanted a prize, so she began.

First she peeked through the fence. "I used my eyes," she said. Then the sheep said, "Baa!" Harper laughed. "My ears heard that!" She touched the wool. It was soft and warm. "That was my hands." Grandpa held out hay. The sheep ate it fast. "It smells good," said Harper, "my nose knows!" Then Grandpa gave her cool water. "My tongue tastes that. That is five!"

Grandpa clapped. He picked her up high. "Eyes, ears, hands, nose, tongue," said Harper. The sheep went "Baa!" one more time.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
In the morning, Layla ran to Grandma's kitchen. The bread was baking. Layla smelled it with her nose. "Grandma, what part do I use to smell?" she asked. "Your nose," said Grandma. Layla laughed. "One! My nose smells the bread."

Grandma gave her a warm slice. Layla touched it with her fingers. "Two! My fingers feel the warm bread." She took a little bite. "Three! My tongue tastes it. Yum." The kitchen window was open. A bird sang outside. "Four! My ears hear the bird," said Layla.

Then she saw her favorite cup on the shelf. "Five! My eyes see my cup." Grandma clapped. "You named all five senses." Layla counted them on her fingers. "Nose, fingers, tongue, ears, eyes. That is five." She put her hands on her cheeks. "The bird sings because the sun is up," she said. Grandma kissed her head.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Matthew got to daycare and saw the play kitchen. It had a little pot and little cups. His friend Emma held a baby doll. The doll was crying, Emma said. Matthew wanted to help the baby.

Emma said the baby was hungry. Matthew looked in the pot. It was empty. So he found some round blocks. He dropped them in. "Soup," he said. He stirred it with a big spoon. He made the spoon go round and round. Then he held it up to the doll's mouth. Emma made eating sounds. "Mmm," said the baby.

The crying stopped. Emma smiled a big smile. Matthew said, "The baby stopped crying because I fed her soup." The teacher gave him a coin for the pretend store. Matthew made the coin go into a tall tower of cups. "One coin, one cake," he said. The teacher bought a pretend cake.

Then Emma handed Matthew the doll. "Your turn to be the dad," she said. Matthew remembered how his own dad patted his back. He patted the doll, soft and slow. The doll went to sleep. "Shh," whispered Matthew.

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
story:
Arthur sat on the big couch. He had a cold. His nose was red. His sock was warm and cozy on his feet.

Mama brought him a cup of water. "Drink a little," she said. Arthur took a sip. Then he took another sip. "My cough went away," he said. "Why did it go away?" Was it because of the water?

Mama tucked a blanket around him. Arthur yawned a big yawn. His eyes felt heavy, like rocks. He let his head rest on the soft pillow. Soon he was asleep. He slept and slept.

When Arthur woke up, he sat up tall. He sniffed with his nose. It was clear now! "Mama, I slept, and now I am better," he said. Mama smiled and gave him an orange. Arthur took a bite. "Ooh, sour!" he said. He made a funny face. Then he wiggled his sock toes and laughed.

"Can we sleep again tomorrow?" he asked.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Oliver was at Grandpa's house. The big game was on TV. Everyone sat on the big couch. Aunt May sat on the arm of the couch. Uncle Ben sat there too. The arm was full.

Oliver had no seat. He wanted to see the TV. Dad said, "The game will not start yet. We can wait." So Oliver waited. He walked around the room. He found a small stool. He carried it to the couch. He set it down in front of Dad. He sat on it.

The game began. The crowd on TV got loud. Everyone cheered. Oliver could see the whole TV now. "My stool made me tall," said Oliver. Grandpa laughed. Then the team scored, and Grandma hugged the lamp by mistake. "That is Grandma's seat," said Oliver, and he patted the stool.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
Today was Victor's birthday. There were balloons on the door. There was paper on the table with bears on it. Grandma came. Mia came too.

Mom set down a big cake. The cake had three candles. "Why three?" asked Victor. "You are three!" said Mom.

Victor took a big breath. He blew and blew. The candles went out. The room got dark for a second. "The candles went out because I blew!" said Victor.

"Make a wish and choose your first piece," said Dad. Victor chose the piece with a bear on it. It was chocolate. It was so good.

Then everyone sang. The singing was very loud. It was not scary at all. It was fun.

Victil clapped and clapped. "Next year I will be four," he said. "Will there be four candles?" "Yes!" said Mia.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
story:
Brielle stood at school with a red beanbag. Her teacher, a kind woman, put a hoop on the floor. "Throw it in," said the woman. Brielle threw it very hard. The beanbag flew over the hoop. It landed far away.

Brielle got it back. She tried again, very hard. Over the hoop it went again. She sat down. "Too far," she said.

Then she looked at the hoop. It was close. She threw the beanbag soft and low. It went in! "Soft throw goes in," said Brielle. The woman clapped.

Next came a big ball. A boy named Sam rolled it to her. Brielle held out one hand. The big ball hit her hand and bounced off. It rolled into the block tower. The tower fell down. Sam looked angry. His face was red and his mouth turned down.

"I can fix it," said Brielle. She helped Sam build the tower again. Block by block, up it went. Sam smiled. Then the woman said, "Two hands for a big ball." Brielle held out both hands. Sam rolled the ball. She held it with both hands. She caught it! "Both hands hold the big ball," said Brielle.

Sam rolled it again. Brielle caught it once more. Then she rolled it back, soft and low.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Natalie was four. She played soccer at the big park. Her team was called the Red Apples. On game day, every player got a red shirt to wear.

One day, Natalie did not wear her red shirt. She wore her blue shirt. She ran onto the grass. She kicked the ball. Then a boy took the ball away from her. Another girl took it too. Natalie stopped and frowned. There were so many kids. She could not tell who was on her team.

A shy boy named Sam tugged her hand. He pointed at his own red shirt. Then he pointed at the red shirts near the goal. Natalie looked down at her blue shirt. Then she looked at the red shirts. She saw it. The kids in red passed to each other. The kids in blue passed to each other. "The shirt shows the team," she said.

Coach Maya had the extra red shirt. Natalie put it on. She ran back out. Sam passed the ball to her. Natalie kicked it, kick, kick, kick. A little ant crawled by her shoe. She stepped over it and kept running. Then she kicked the ball into the net. Goal!

The Red Apples all jumped up and down. Sam gave Natalie a big hug. "Red shirts stick together," said Natalie. She ran back to the middle of the field, ready for the next kick.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
story:
Maya stood in the school hallway. Her hand held Papa's hand tight. The hallway was long and empty. Maya did not know where to put her bag.

Papa walked with her to the wall. There were little doors with names. Maya saw an M. She looked closer. It said MAYA. "That is my name," she said. She hung her bag on the hook. The hook caught the strap and held it. "My name shows my spot," said Maya.

One shoe felt bumpy. Maya took it off. Sand fell out on the floor. The sand came from the beach yesterday. It fell out because the shoe was full of sand. Maya tipped the other shoe too. More sand fell out. A teacher came with a small broom. "I will sweep it," she said. "Then come paint with us, Maya." Maya smiled and took Papa's hand one more time. Papa kissed her head. Then Maya ran to the paint table.
